### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **67** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-only-local-password.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**39** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-only-local-password.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 54 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d9161a65b18001a926eb90fbdacce4ef89784c82` — the merge of head `b60bbe40fd7842664c4fdc94a2546130e30dd739` into base `162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d9161a65b18001a926eb90fbdacce4ef89784c82 && git checkout d9161a65b18001a926eb90fbdacce4ef89784c82
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf b60bbe40fd7842664c4fdc94a2546130e30dd739 && git checkout -B drift-repro 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf && git merge --no-ff b60bbe40fd7842664c4fdc94a2546130e30dd739

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · REWORK (L1, first read) · Head-sha: 9b95ba90952671756cb99a439b31a4a99aa0be20 · 2026-11-16T10:22Z

L1 thread L1-a for area o1-A, on the final head declared in 6913652042. Read: card #34257, the PR body, and the full diff against merge base `951eceee` (36 files, +1897/−24). Not governed by size; Tier H by `docs/adr/0138-*`. The L2 record at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is review#1's and is not repeated here.

### What holds

- **The proof.** Minted per send in `sendInvitationEmail` through the request's internal adapter, a resend deleting the old row first. Only the SHA-256, the lowercased address and the expiry are stored. Checked with `constantTimeEqual`, and spent by the adapter's atomic consume after every refusal point, with the consumed row's hash compared to the read one, so a concurrent second redeemer is refused.
- **Deliver-only mail.** `sendTemplate` renders the stored faces from `data` alone and hands the transport a second render with `deliverOnly` overlaid. `acceptUrl` is a top-level template variable (`auth-templates.ts`), so the shallow overlay reaches it. A deliver-only send is forced inline (`allowQueue = false`). The copy action is untouched.
- **Ordering.** Rate limit, then invitation pending, then proof admits, then the `sign_in` fallbacks, then the password gates, then hash, then consume, then writes. Every proof refusal is the one `400 INVALID_TOKEN`.
- **Card items 1–5 each map to code.** The page reads the proof from the fragment and clears it with `replaceState`. The provider return redeems in session mode, which requires the invited address and `emailVerified === true`.
- **The changeset sentences match the code.** Checked: the deliver-only and inline rule; the copy link without the proof; the door's one-request behaviour and session revoke; `INVALID_TOKEN` uniformity; the `sign_in` cases; `verify_email`; the page's fragment handling. On SSO-only: a new address is refused through the forced `disableSignUp`, and an existing one answers `sign_in` via `isSsoOnlyMode()`.
- **The pinned refusals assert both `status` and `code`.** The proof refusal asserts `400` with `INVALID_TOKEN`, and the rate limit asserts `429` with `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

### Must

1. **Pin the gates the body and changeset claim.** The 16 door tests pin the proof rules, the verified and linked-provider `sign_in` cases, the session modes and the rate limit. The other claimed gates of this unauthenticated, account-creating door have no test and no ablation leg. Each new case asserts `status` and `code` (or the `sign_in` outcome), that nothing was written, and that the real proof is still redeemable afterwards. Ablate each one. The cases:
   - email sign-up switched off (`disableSignUp`), for a new address;
   - SSO-only mode, for a new address and for an existing unverified one;
   - an existing unverified account with a second factor;
   - an existing unverified account that is directory-managed (IdP-provisioned, and pending-SSO);
   - a password under the minimum length;
   - a password the complexity check refuses (the `globalBeforeHook` path added here);
   - a breached password: this is the claim that hashing before the consume leaves the proof usable;
   - an audience-admission refusal;
   - a new address with no name.
2. **The cloud-managed posture.** `cloud-managed.ts` states the rule that every door that sets a local password is closed on a cloud-managed environment (ruling 10 of objectstack-ai/cloud#4465, #33203). This door sets one on an existing unverified account and does not ask `isCloudManaged()`. Today a new address there is refused only through the forced `disableSignUp`, as `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, not the posture's `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`.
   - Fix: apply the existing rule at the door. Refuse proof mode with the cloud-managed refusal, adding the door to `cloud-managed.ts`'s list and its docblock. Pin it for a new address and for an existing unverified one, with its ablation.
   - If the area reads this as anything other than applying the existing ruling (for example, if the hosted consumer cloud#4470 needs the door open on a managed environment), stop and take it to the seat. ⛔ Not decided in the PR.

### Should

1. The anonymous session-mode case (`anonymous.status` 401) asserts no `code`. Assert `UNAUTHENTICATED` too.
2. The ADR-0138 note and the route-ledger note both say "per-address" rate limit. The code keys on the client's network address (`readRequestClientAddress`), not the invited mail address. Write "per client address" in both, as the body and changeset already do.
3. The acceptance notes cover a vendor-accept failure after the consume. Add the same sentence for a write that fails after the consume (account create or link, password update): the proof is spent and the person uses the link without it.

### Not read this round

Gate check-runs are not re-read: the verdict is REWORK, and the next head brings its own runs. The area's 6913652042 records every run on this head as success or path-skipped.

After the fix round, I read only the delta.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9b95ba90952671756cb99a439b31a4a99aa0be20`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts, docs/adr/0138-guest-model-anonymous-principal-doors-grants-and-organization.md + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/invitation-mailbox-proof.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-organization-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-plugin-list.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-route-ledger.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/email-service.ts, scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs, ui/packages/auth/src/createAuthClient.ts, ui/packages/auth/src/AuthContext.ts, ui/packages/auth/src/AuthProvider.tsx, ui/packages/auth/src/types.ts, ui/packages/auth/src/useAuth.ts, ui/packages/auth/src/index.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/organizations/manage/AcceptInvitationPage.tsx
Security-touching: yes

Read: card #34257 with every comment, the PR body and comments, the net diff against `origin/main`, the check-runs on this head (every run success or skipped), and the rule text on `main`. The vendor package is not installed in the reviewing checkout, so vendor behaviour is taken from the tree's own comments and the green runs, not from its source. Findings on the door are stated as rules only.

### ① Derived judgments

- `SendTemplateInput.deliverOnly`: one optional key, a widening. The one in-repo implementation enforces it: the row is rendered from `data` alone, the transport gets the overlay, and the send is forced inline. No caller-facing door forwards a caller object into `sendTemplate`; the plugin-auth callers, `mail-tenant-currency.ts` and the messaging email channel each build the input themselves. An implementation that ignores the key delivers the row's faces, which is the safe direction.
- One new route on the auth catch-all, with its ledger row and its mounted-surface entry. `source: 'better-auth'` is right by the ledger's own definition (a row verified against the live `auth.api` table).
- `@object-ui/auth` gains `acceptInvitationWithProof` and two exported types on the client, the context and `useAuth`. The accept page consumes them.
- The door joins the complexity before-hook, the breach-check path list and the operator rate-limit rules. The invitation mail moves from the configured delivery mode to inline delivery.
- Previously accepted, now refused: none found in the tree. One hunk could not be settled from the tree; see S5.

S6 (should-fix) — The route and the client method are named for the proof, and both also serve a mode that carries none (a signed-in session). The name is wrong for that mode, and a published route cannot be renamed later without a break. The follow-up that makes the vendor accept route require a verified address covers the same ground. Split the session mode out, or name the door for what both modes do.

N1 (nit) — `deliverOnly` reads as a mode switch beside its sibling `data`, and it holds data. The outcome `verify_email` is also answered to a session whose address is simply not the invited one.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on all six packages, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset. `SendTemplateInput` is a programmatic contract interface, not something a metadata author writes, so the kind is `none`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md, post-task step 3). Holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in the report.
- Deviation, `deliverOnly` on `SendTemplateInput` only: answered, holds. `SendEmailInput` has no render step for the key to act on, and the caller-facing doors keep their shape.
- Deviation, registered codes in place of the vendor's sign-up codes: answered, holds. The door is new and its codes are in the catalog.
- Deviation, the envelope and the `PLUGIN_ROUTE_MODULES` declaration: answered. A success is the envelope; a refusal is the vendor's raised error. The client reads both shapes.
- Deviation, not run locally: answered by the green check-runs on this head.
- Deviation, gate-touched files: answered. The pinned ledger records coverage and may only grow, and the envelope entry declares no departure.
- Escalated, not answered here: the refinement of ruling 6413975861 Q2 B that the ADR note states. It is the maintainer's, on the Tier H hand-off.
- The cloud fact asked on the card is answered there by the cloud seat (6913807072): hosted acceptance runs outside managed environments. M1 follows from it.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The door reads one invitation, one user with its accounts, one source and one verification row.

S5 (should-fix) — The breach-check plugin is now handed an explicit path list described as the vendor's own default plus this door. That equality is not pinned and could not be read here. If the vendor's default is shorter, other password doors gain a refusal under a widening declaration; if the vendor later extends it, the copy silently loses the addition. Pin the list against the vendor's default.

### ④ Design judgment

**The contract, `packages/spec/src/contracts/email-service.ts`.** Against its first consumer, the invitation send, it holds: the mail carries the value, the stored row does not, and no log line or preview reads the delivered faces. `LogTransport` logs no body, and a failed delivery stores only the transport's error text.

N2 (nit) — The stored row gives no sign that deliver-only values were overlaid, while `email-service.ts` still calls the row the record of what was sent. Record on the row that an overlay was applied (key names only), or say in the contract that the row gives no sign.

N3 (nit) — The contract does not say that required variables are checked against `data` alone. The invitation mail also gives up durable queue delivery where a queue is mounted; the changeset says so under the contract bullet only.

**The ADR note, `docs/adr/0138-…`.**

M3 (must-fix) — The note says the door "is classified under class 2 the way the preview above is". The tree does not hold that: `packages/qa/dogfood/test/anonymous-door-sweep.classification.ts` carries the preview's row and nothing for this door or for the client-name read, and the diff touches nothing there. As D2's own preview note explains, a route in the auth namespace without such a row is claimed by the allowlist family and the sweep judges nothing. Add the classification and its expectation, or state what does hold.

S3 (should-fix) — The note's "per-address" rate limit reads as the invited address, the sense "address" has everywhere else in the note; the code keys on the client's network address. The ledger note has the same wording. The note also cites a seat's claim amendment as its authority while refining a maintainer ruling; cite the maintainer's approval once it is given.

N4 (nit) — For the client-name read, "every other request gets one uniform 404" leaves out the malformed-request and over-limit answers that `oauth-client-name.ts` gives.

**The implementing files.** The proof is bound to the invitation, its address and its expiry. It is stored only as a digest, in a column the generic reads strip. A resend retires it. A proof that does not match is not spent, and no other account can use it. The copy action and the stored mail row do not carry it. Three rules on `main` are not held by the door:

M1 (must-fix) — `cloud-managed.ts` on `main`: every door that sets a local password is closed on a cloud-managed environment, and each door asks the posture itself. This door sets a local password and does not ask. Today it is kept shut there only because another door refuses upstream. Apply the existing refusal at the door, and name the door in the lists of `cloud-managed.ts` and `sso-only-local-password.ts`. The cloud seat's answer on the card means this takes nothing from the first consumer.

M2 (must-fix) — ADR-0069 D1 attaches after-effects to a password set at the sign-up and reset doors: the password-age stamp and the forced-change clear (`auth-manager-after-hook.ts`). This door sets a password, on a new account and on an existing one, and writes neither, so the password-age rule does not start for it. Run the same after-effects, and pin them.

S1 (should-fix) — Single-use is stated as an atomic consume in the module doc, the ADR note and the changeset. The tree holds it against sequential reuse only; the store's consume on the platform's own adapter does not give the guarantee the text states under concurrent redemption. Bound the claim, or make the door hold it, and pin a concurrent case. (Rule level only; the detail is with the seat.)

S2 (should-fix) — The changeset states gates no test pins: sign-up switched off, SSO-only, second factor, directory-managed source, password length, complexity, breach, audience admission, a missing name, and the per-client-address window. Each is present in the code as read. Each needs a pin asserting status, code, that nothing was written, and that the proof stays usable.

S4 (should-fix) — The arm that takes over an unverified account lists the account states that fall back to sign-in, with no stated closing rule and no pin of its completeness. The sessions it ends also leave no revoke reason: the door is not in `session-tombstone.ts#INTERACTIVE_REVOKE_REASON`, where every reset door is. State the rule, add the door to that ledger, and pin both. A security item on this arm is with the owner seat.

N5 (nit) — With no client address established, every caller shares one window, and a holder of the invitation id can exhaust that invitation's window. A banned unverified account has its password replaced before the session refusal answers. `auth-plugin.ts` spells the door's path as a literal where the module exports a constant.

The UI consumers agree with the door. The page takes the proof out of its address on first read and keeps it in memory only. The provider return carries no proof and redeems in session mode. A link without the proof keeps today's path. The client accepts only the three declared outcomes and keeps a refusal's code and status.
